summary: This House resolution supports designating May 4-8 2026 as Teacher Appreciation Week and calls on federal state and local leaders to give teachers a direct role in education policy decisions.

scores.thoughts: The resolution highlights teacher support for maintaining federal funding under Title I and IDEA as well as a fully staffed Department of Education. While it does not enact spending changes, it endorses continued federal education expenditures, creating a minor link to expanding or sustaining government spending.
No references to tax policy, rates, or revenue measures appear in the bill text.
The bill contains no provisions or statements related to healthcare systems, coverage, or markets.
No content addresses firearms, regulations, or Second Amendment issues.
The resolution cites teacher support for the right of undocumented students to attend public school, which aligns with expanding protections and pathways for immigrants.
No mention of reproductive rights or abortion policy.
The bill does not discuss military or defense budgets or policy.
No environmental or climate-related provisions are present.
The text does not address welfare programs, food assistance, or similar safety-net policies.

The resolution strongly endorses public school teachers, federal education funding (Title I, IDEA), the Department of Education, and reserving public funds exclusively for public schools while opposing privatization signals. This directly advances public-school investment and federal involvement.
No references to drug enforcement, decriminalization, or related policies.
The bill contains no criminal-justice or policing provisions.
No trade, tariff, or globalization content is included.
The resolution does not address deficits, debt reduction, or fiscal priorities.
It cites overwhelming teacher support for federal protections against discrimination based on gender and sexual identity, aligning with expanded legal protections for LGBTQ+ individuals.
No foreign-aid provisions appear.
The bill does not discuss voting access, election integrity, or related reforms.
A single clause notes teacher support for safely leveraging AI in classrooms, but this is incidental and does not engage regulatory or privacy policy.
By championing public-school teachers and their role in policy, the resolution indirectly supports a heavily unionized workforce, though it stops short of explicit union provisions.
The resolution endorses federal anti-discrimination protections covering gender and sexual identity, which tilts toward prioritizing civil-rights protections over religious exemptions.
